item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00269","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C12","C19","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C12","confidence":0.97,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C12 provides a highly specific drafting template: identify an earlier tariff proclamation, explain that a product was inadvertently not excluded from a schedule item, invoke section 350 authority to terminate the earlier proclamation in part, and direct that it be applied as though the corrected item text had been stated. The child repeats this unusual factual and operative sequence for fruit juices and also adds a second textual correction. C19 is a strong correction precedent but lacks the distinctive inadvertent-exclusion rationale; C08 shares the partial-termination and 'applied as though' machinery but uses it for an injury-based tariff withdrawal.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the said item 806 (a) was not intended to cover citrus fruit juices, but such juices other than naranjilla juice inadvertently were not excepted","parent_excerpt":"the first subdivision of the item specified in the third recital of this proclamation was not intended to cover chamois leather, but such leather inadvertently was not excluded","explanation":"Distinctive parallel explanation that an item unintentionally covered a product because the product was inadvertently omitted from an exclusion."},{"child_excerpt":"the said [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 13, 1956, is hereby terminated, to the extent that it shall be applied as though the description of products in item 806 (a) ... were stated as follows","parent_excerpt":"the said proclamation of June 2, 1951 is hereby terminated in part, to the extent that ... it shall be applied as though item 1530(c) ... were stated as follows","explanation":"Nearly identical operative machinery and phrasing for partially terminating a prior proclamation and substituting corrected schedule language."},{"child_excerpt":"acting under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the Statutes, including section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended","parent_excerpt":"acting under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the statutes, including the said section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended","explanation":"The same authority clause reinforces the close drafting relationship, although it is less probative standing alone."}]}
